study.title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction Scoring: A Timely Proof-of-Principle Study

imaging.modality_detail: Time-resolved X-ray DSA series, frontal and lateral views, acquired during mechanical thrombectomy
imaging.territory_detail: Middle cerebral artery territory; M1 occlusions in acute ischemic stroke

public_dataset_used.detail: In-house dataset (UKE Hamburg, 491 series/236 patients) and external dataset from the NEUROSQUAD study (95 series/61 patients)

data_released.detail: Data available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request

annotation.annotator_expertise: Neuroradiologists (>5 years experience); in-house scores from clinical reports reviewed by one neuroradiologist, external data rescored by 2 neuroradiologists with consensus
annotation.inter_rater_value: Cohen's kappa 0.75 between the 2 in-house experts on the external dataset

task.task_description: Fully automated mTICI reperfusion scoring (0/1, 2a, 2b, 3; plus dichotomized <=2a vs >=2b) of biplane DSA series after mechanical thrombectomy for M1 occlusions, modeled as ordinal regression.
task.clinical_application: Objective assessment of mechanical thrombectomy success in acute ischemic stroke

temporal_evidence.quote: the developed DL system builds on gated recurrent units[33] (GRU; a specific type of recurrent neural networks)

evaluation.external_validation_detail: Independent external dataset (NEUROSQUAD study, 95 DSA series of 61 patients, different center): direct application (exp. II) and after model updating with 3-fold cross validation (exp. III)

comparators: Published inter-/intrarater variability of expert TICI scoring
Agreement of 2 in-house experts on the external dataset

model_weights_available.detail: The final DL network is available at https://github.com/IPMI-ICNS-UKE/DeepTICI

G1.quote: the main limitations of the present proof-of-principle study are the strict patient selection criteria and the limited size of the resulting dataset

G2.quote: A direct application of the DL model trained on the in-house dataset to the external dataset revealed nevertheless a drop of the prediction accuracy for the different center data.

G3.quote: algorithms capable of exploiting the inherent information of temporal DSA series have been rarely reported on as of yet

G5.quote: the medical expert-based scoring for cases close to mTICI-inherent reperfusion thresholds is not as reliable as ideally desired for training of neural networks

G7.quote: This, in turn, leads to the active field of explainable artificial intelligence and corresponding methodical developments.

G9.quote: especially with regard to the mTICI 1 and 2a classes that were, due to their lower clinical frequency, underrepresented in our in-house dataset

G11.quote: the investigation of the system outputs with respect to clinical questions like correlation to patient outcome will be the next steps of our future work

other_limitations: Restricted to M1 occlusions with strict selection criteria
Lowest performance for mTICI 2b; cases near the 2a/2b threshold
Cannot yet handle additional pathologies, foreign materials or image artifacts
Model update based on only 31-32 DSA series per fold
future_work: Extend to other occlusion sites and expanded TICI
Consensus rating by multiple experts for training labels
Analyze class probabilities or network ensembles to estimate uncertainty
Model updating or data debiasing for new centers
Correlate system outputs with clinical outcome (e.g. mRS, NIHSS)
